clue.text: Tiny part from a male cat

parts.note: taken as written
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone finds a minute fragment that has come off a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest particle of an element, so a tiny constituent part.

clue.text: Addition to book — a page to finish in pictures

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another word, between its letters

parts.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for page
pix is informal for pictures
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: An editor adds a final illustrated page to a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Pix is informal plural slang for pictures or photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is supplementary material added at the back of a book.

clue.text: Round hole is egg-shaped

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape
a void is an empty space or gap

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a round opening is actually oval.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid comes from the Latin for egg and describes an oval, egg-like form.

clue.text: Saying something seconds before reaching the top

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for seconds
peaking means hitting the highest point

explanation.surface: Someone says their piece in the last seconds before a climber reaches a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking is the act of uttering words, the present participle matching the phrase about saying something.

clue.text: Walk one in pram, mostly before noon

indicators.note: placed ahead of something, so one piece comes earlier than the next
one piece is placed inside the other word
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: pram is short for perambulator, a baby carriage
I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A parent goes for a stroll, pushing a child in a pram before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Pram is a shortening of PERAMBULATOR; drop its final R, slip I in before its last O, then add N.
explanation.definitionFit: A perambulation is a leisurely stroll, a formal word for a walk.

clue.text: Book of maps a sailor's taken up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue taking something up lifts it, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor has picked up a book of charts.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps.

clue.text: Made from lava energy using oxygen to mix

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A volcano stirs energy and oxygen together to produce rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous rock forms when molten magma or lava cools and solidifies.

clue.text: Beginning to get cheap light radiation

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the first letter of this word
low prices are cheap ones

explanation.surface: Starting to get inexpensive lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A glow is a steady emission of light, especially from something warm.

clue.text: Lover's song — no advert for calm

indicators.note: saying no to something means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: a serenade is sung by a lover beneath a window
ad is short for advert

explanation.surface: A love song free of commercial breaks makes for a calm mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AD out of SERENADE. An advert is the British word for an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene means peaceful and untroubled, a synonym of calm as an adjective.

clue.text: Prepare unit to invade landing stage

indicators.note: an invader goes inside territory, so one piece pushes into the middle of the other

parts.note: a pier is a structure where boats land
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: Orders to ready a military unit to storm a jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare' is the definition in its verb sense: to pioneer is to prepare the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer is to open up or lay the groundwork for something new, preparing the way for others.

clue.text: Language that's a part of Klingon

indicators.note: the answer is only a portion of the next word, sitting inside it

parts.note: the letters run from the second to the sixth of this word

explanation.surface: A Star Trek fan notes that a certain language belongs to the Klingons.
explanation.walkthrough: Klingon is itself a language from Star Trek, which makes the hidden word neatly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is an informal word for a language or jargon, especially a foreign or unfamiliar one.

clue.text: Elbow's bare, broken by golf

indicators.note: something broken into has another item thrust into its middle

parts.note: nude means bare, unclothed
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer's arm is exposed and then injured during a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elbow' looks like a noun, a body part, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to nudge them, prodding with the arm.

clue.text: What brings luck millions wanted at racecourse

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for millions
Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A gambler hoping for good fortune wants to win millions at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object believed to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Vision certainly present in a number

indicators.note: being present in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: eight is a number
yes means certainly as an affirmation

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed person certainly sees something in a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, which is what vision means here.

clue.text: Clue is roundly trashed in a cynical manner

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver scornfully pans a crossword clue as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To act incredulously is to show disbelief, which is how a cynic or skeptic responds.

clue.text: Stuff about even pieces of antique skull

parts.note: to cram is to stuff full

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, second, fourth and sixth, are the ones kept

parts.note: letters two, four and six of this word

explanation.surface: Packing an old relic's skull with stuffing.
explanation.definitionFit: The cranium is the part of the skull enclosing the brain.

clue.text: Method of printing's not working on gel

parts.note: a machine that is off is not working
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: A printing process fails because of something to do with gel.
explanation.definitionFit: Offset is a printing technique where ink transfers from plate to rubber blanket to paper.

clue.text: Country hat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Central American nation
second meaning: a lightweight brimmed straw hat

explanation.walkthrough: Reads as a style of country hat, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is the isthmus republic, and a panama is a straw hat named after goods shipped via that nation.

clue.text: Flooded area was hard

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area; the answer also happens to run through these words, a coincidence the charade does not need
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.definitionFit: Awash means covered or swamped by water.

clue.text: Concentration of force with company backed by United States

parts.note: F is the symbol for force in physics

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so the abbreviation reads from right to left

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.definitionFit: Focus means concentrated attention or effort on one thing.

clue.text: Wipe top of cooker with very little fat on

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of this word
lean meat has hardly any fat on it

explanation.surface: Wiping down a greasy stove top with barely any grease on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A cooker is the British word for a stove.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean something is to wipe away its dirt, so the two verbs are synonyms here.

clue.text: Playing cards in runs? That's not right

indicators.note: not having something means it is removed from the word

parts.note: races are runs, contests of speed
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cricketer suspects a card game is going on during runs, and disapproves.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are the highest-ranking cards in many games, one per suit in a pack.

clue.text: A source of tea cups and saucers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the country, a major tea grower

explanation.definitionFit: The country is where tea originated and is still widely grown, and fine porcelain tableware is called by the same name.

clue.text: Vast amount of hard water ruined beer in one hundred gallons

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other group of letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: ruined beer has gone bad, so its letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written, then rearranged
G is an abbreviation for gallons

explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged beer sits between I C and G.

clue.text: My son sent back bogus musical work

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son
phony means fake or bogus

explanation.surface: A parent returns a fake piece of music their son bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is an extended orchestral composition, a substantial musical work.

clue.text: King with no time for granny?

definitions.note: a definition by example, flagged by the question mark

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A king too busy to spend time with his grandmother.
